lines.text: You burned it.
Day ten. Antarctica. And you are, genuinely, the safest person alive.
For about four more hours.
Minus sixty outside. They freeze solid in under two minutes.
Rule one. Shelter.
Built for forty. Sealed against a hundred-mile wind. Check.
lines.cap:
BUILT FOR FORTY. SEALED
AGAINST A 100-MILE WIND.

lines.text: Rule two. Food.
A year of frozen stores. Ten thousand gallons of fuel. Water, lying on the ground. Check.
lines.cap:
A YEAR OF STORES.
10,000 GALLONS OF FUEL.

lines.text: Rule three. Cold.
You switch off the runway lights. Nothing finds you from the air. Check.
lines.cap:
LIGHTS OFF. NOTHING FINDS
YOU FROM THE AIR.

lines.text: On paper, you have thought of everything.
Then Priya picks up your radio. And turns it over.
lines.cap:
PRIYA PICKS UP YOUR RADIO.
AND TURNS IT OVER.

lines.text: And asks why a receiver has an aerial.
It's a two-way set. Every time you cranked it to listen—
lines.cap:
IT'S A TWO-WAY SET.
EVERY TIME YOU CRANKED IT—

lines.text: Day one, the traffic. Day three, the service station. Day five, the signal box—
You were transmitting.
The loop was never a broadcast. It was someone answering you.
For ten days, you've told something exactly where you are. Four hours ago, you told it where you'll be all winter.
lines.cap:
FOR TEN DAYS, YOU TOLD IT
EXACTLY WHERE YOU ARE.

lines.text: Outside, the runway lights come back on. By themselves.
lines.cap:
THE LIGHTS COME BACK ON.
BY THEMSELVES.

lines.text: You were never following the signal. It was following you.
